messages:
oliver: Heads up — I found a scope enforcement glitch in staging. An embeddings-only API key successfully completed a chat request to /v1/chat/complete. Repro steps below.

oliver: Repro (staging):
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-emb-xxxx' -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/complete -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'
```
Response: 200 + tokens generated. Logged token_id=tok_7a1f in audit log.

priya: yikes. did it hit the auth middleware or bypass the route-level check? any stack traces?

oliver: it looks like the route-level scope check returned 403 for model selection, but the code path that proxies to the legacy chat_backend uses a separate token validation path that only checks existence, not scope. stack snippet: `if (token && token.active) next()` — missing `token.allows('chat')`.

aj: I'll take a look. this smells like the refactor from last quarter where we split validation between gateway and service. maybe a missing header propagation or different validator instance.

sam: assign to aj. in the meantime, can we revoke the affected key and rotate? what does audit show about other calls from that token?

audit-bot: audit-log: token_id=tok_7a1f, created_by=maria, scopes=[embeddings.create], last_used=1772345601, ips=[10.23.4.8], requests=[/v1/embeddings, /v1/chat/complete]

maria: that token was issued for analytics pipeline. we can rotate but pipeline will fail until we update. we need a short mitigation window.

priya: mitigation plan: (1) emergency ACL rule: block tokens with `embeddings.*` from chat routes at the gateway (fast rollback), (2) patch chat_backend token validator to enforce `scope.includes('chat')` (hotfix), (3) rotate the affected token and notify teams. aj can you open a PR for (2)?)

aj: on it. I'll add a middleware test and unit tests for both gateway and chat_backend. PR: https://git.internal.redwood/infrasec/pr/4920 (draft)

oliver: also found a few audit gaps — last_used recorded, but we don't capture `route_intent` (embeddings vs chat) in KMS-wrapped audit entries. suggestion: include `request_intent` and `model_type` in audit logs for easier triage.

sam: agree. file a ticket for audit enrichment. we should also log `token_derived_from` when rotation happens (to track which service created a rotated key).

priya: I'll file INC-2026 for the incident and ENR-789 for audit changes. add severity P2 now since user impact limited to staging and one pipeline.

maria: for the rotation: can we do a key alias in KMS so pipeline can switch without secret leaks? we use aws:kms alias pattern for env secrets.

aj: we need to be careful: rotation path calls KMS to rewrap; ensure old wrapped key is revoked. I'll add a cleanup job to delete old ciphertext blobs after 24h.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/hotfix/scope-check -> staging, build 2026-03-19_14:12. smoke tests pending.

oliver: smoke: blocked chat with embeddings key now returns 403. good. patch passed basic e2e but need more load testing.

priya: next steps: 1) aj finish PR and get review (priority), 2) sam coordinate KMS rotation with pipeline owners, 3) priya/oliver update runbook on scope enforcement, include new auditing fields, 4) maria schedule key rotation window. I'll own communications.

aj: PR updated with unit tests and integration test simulating token types. pinged @platform for review.

maria: doing rotation at 23:00 UTC, will post outage window. will use alias switch to minimize downtime.

priya: thanks team. capture retrospective notes after rotation. add a postmortem only if we see recurrence or production impact. :white_check_mark:
